title: the Shiva Purana (selections)
hook: spring arrives on Shiva's mountain out of season, and Kama, the god of desire, takes aim at the god who is deep in meditation

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Shiva Purana, Sati would not hear her husband mocked, and a proud father got a goat's head and a second chance. Did you speak up for anyone? Today closes a week. Day one thousand one hundred twenty.
screen: `A FAMILY QUARREL SHAKES THE WORLD.` · `A THIRD SELECTION.`

segments.voice: On a frozen mountainside, the snow starts to melt. Out of season, trees burst into flower. Bees show up. A cuckoo starts singing. The breeze turns warm and sweet. Every living thing on the mountain feels it. Except one. Under a tree, Shiva sits in meditation, perfectly still, eyes closed, as if spring were somebody else's business. And hiding behind a bush, with a bow made of sugarcane and arrows tipped with flowers, crouches Kama, the god of desire. He's been sent on a mission, and he's nervous.
screen: `SPRING, OUT OF SEASON.` → `SHIVA, PERFECTLY STILL.` → `KAMA TAKES AIM.`

segments.voice: Here's why he's there. Since Sati gave up her body, Shiva has withdrawn into meditation. Sati has been born again as Parvati, the daughter of the mountain king, and she comes every day to serve him: flowers, water, a clean place to sit. He doesn't look up. Meanwhile, the gods are in trouble. A demon named Taraka has a boon, and in the Shiva Purana only a son of Shiva can defeat him. So the gods need Shiva to marry, and Shiva is busy being still. Indra, king of the gods, has a plan. Send Kama. Send Spring with him. Desire will do what persuasion can't. Kama waits for his moment, Parvati standing near, and lets an arrow fly. And for a moment it works. Shiva's mind stirs. He opens his eyes and looks at Parvati. Then he catches himself and looks around for the cause, and sees Kama with his bow. Fire bursts from Shiva's third eye, and Kama is burned to ash on the spot. The path met the far end of this story earlier, in a hymn to the goddess; here is how it began. Rati, Kama's wife, falls weeping beside the ashes, and in the story she's promised that her husband will live again. The plan has failed. Shiva leaves. Parvati goes home. Notice what this selection teaches by failing. Help from outside, spring, flowers, an arrow, couldn't win Shiva. Desire forced in from outside burned up. Whatever wins him will have to come from Parvati herself. And that closes a week that held a lot of fire: the last nights of Navaratri, the honest god at the pillar of flame, Sati at her father's sacrifice, and now the third eye opening.
screen: `PARVATI SERVES; SHIVA IS STILL.` · `THE GODS SEND DESIRE.` · `THE THIRD EYE OPENS.` · `IT CAN'T BE FORCED FROM OUTSIDE.` · then, large: `KAMA, BURNED TO ASH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: let a want pass by. Settle, and let the breath slow. Sit as still as you comfortably can. Sooner or later a want will show up, small or big: to check your phone, to eat something, to be somewhere else, to have something you don't. When it comes, don't fight it and don't follow it. Just notice: there's a want. Watch it rise, and watch it fall, the way spring went on all around a still figure under a tree. Then come back to the breath. If you pray, you can say Shiva's name, or the name of God you use, as you come back. The bell holds the time.
The Shiva Purana. Today's selection: Kama sent with spring to stir Shiva, and burned to ash by the third eye. Desire forced in from outside can't win him.
Your line: the Shiva Purana, in selections. Today, catch one want as it arises, and let it pass once without acting on it. Day one thousand one hundred twenty. A week, kept.

howItsDone: Hindus tell the burning of Kama in the Shiva Purana and in poetry and dance; Shiva is often shown with a third eye on his forehead, and in some places the story is remembered at Holi or in spring festivals.
